data.name: Reuvenos
data.gender_notes: Reuvenos is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Reuvenos is derived from the Hebrew name Reuben, which means 'son of Jacob' or 'friend of Jacob'. In the Old Testament, Reuben is the eldest son of Jacob and Leah. He was born when Jacob had a dream about a 'little son coming up from his feet' (Genesis 29:32). As the eldest son, Reuben was given the birthright and the double portion of the inheritance. However, he lost his birthright because he disobeyed his father's instructions and slept with his father's concubine, Bilhah (Genesis 49:3-4). Despite this, Reuben is still an important figure in Jewish and Christian tradition. His name is a reminder of God's promises and the importance of obedience.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes friendship and loyalty, particularly between a father and his eldest son.
data.etymology: Reuvenos belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of Jacob.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Reuvenos total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Reuvenos has strong cultural significance in Jewish and Christian tradition, as it is derived from the name of Jacob's eldest son, Reuben. This name carries the legacy of Reuben's release from the bondage of Egypt with his family under the leadership of Moses (Exodus 4:28-31). In Eastern Christianity, Reuben is considered to be one of the three holy young men, the Anapauros or Anatolios, who were found to be still alive in the furnace, miraculously preserved by God. They were subsequently honored as saints in both Eastern and Western Churches.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Reuvenos holds significant spiritual meaning in Christianity, as it reminds us of God's faithfulness and promises. Despite Reuben's disobedience and the resulting loss of the birthright, God still considered him an important part of His plan. The name is an encouragement to remain faithful to God, even in the face of difficulties, and reminds us of the importance of obedience, as God's promises remain steadfast despite our mistakes. Additionally, the name carries a reminder of God's power to preserve and protect His children, as evidenced by the story of the three holy young men in the furnace.

His works were collected and published posthumously under the title 'The Reubenos Commentaries'.

Reuben was a disciple of St. Silouan of Athos and is considered to be a major figures in the development of Russian spirituality.
